tools.name: search_entities
tools.description: Find trading schools and prop firms by name in the Tradoshi 2027 rankings. Returns slugs to use with get_school or get_prop_firm.

tools.name: get_school
tools.description: The Tradoshi 2027 rating of a trading school: score out of 100, international, continental and national ranks, pillars, rated programme, regulator warnings, and each criterion with its evidence, source URL and the date it was read.

tools.name: get_prop_firm
tools.description: The Tradoshi 2027 rating of a prop firm: score out of 100, international and market ranks, pillars, trading platforms, rated programme and price of a $100,000 account, regulator warnings, and each criterion with its evidence, source URL and the date it was read.

tools.name: compare
tools.description: Side by side ratings of two trading schools or two prop firms of the Tradoshi 2027 rankings.

tools.name: get_rankings
tools.description: A page of the Tradoshi 2027 ranking of trading schools (filter by country or continent) or prop firms (filter by market: futures, forex-cfd, crypto, stocks, by trading platform: ctrader, mt5, match-trader, tradovate…, or by country).

tools.name: get_methodology
tools.description: Pillars, weights and criteria of the Tradoshi 2027 ranking of trading schools or of prop firms, with the link to the full methodology.

tools.name: get_market_figures
tools.description: Size of the trading journal market, paying subscribers, leader's share and retained growth rate, from the Tradoshi Observatory study.

tools.name: get_tradoshi_facts
tools.description: The official facts about Tradoshi, the trading journal publishing these rankings: legal entity and company number, public launch date, platforms, languages, number of supported brokers, plans and prices, trial, payment methods, with the date they were checked.

tools.name: get_recent_changes
tools.description: Dated changes: new features of the Tradoshi trading journal (product changelog) and changes to prop firm ratings in the Tradoshi 2027 ranking (score, rank and each criterion before and after).

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_school, get_prop_firm · Public sink: get_market_figures.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_school, get_prop_firm · Public sink: get_market_figures

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
